current.text: He is not in the projected starting five (Trae Young, Kyshawn George, AJ Dybantsa, Anthony Davis, Alex Sarr). The fifth starter spot is not settled, and many wings compete for it.
His defense makes him a candidate to start at shooting guard. In past seasons the team always put him back in the lineup after injuries.
Washington has a crowded group of wings and guards. A 10 or 11 man rotation is expected, with 12 or 13 players who could justify minutes.
Trae Young, Anthony Davis and AJ Dybantsa joined the team and will share most of the usage, which cuts into the roles of the young players.
He blocked 26.2% of the rim shots he contested. With Anthony Davis and Alex Sarr around, he is likely to get fewer minutes and fewer rim contests, and his block rate could fall toward average.
Washington is trying to compete this season, so the late-season rest and minutes cuts of past years should not return.
Head coach Brian Keefe is under the most pressure to win games this season.

durable.text: He is a good shot-blocking wing and shows some flashes as a passer. His blocks are high for a guard or forward.
His three-point percentage fell from 34% as a rookie to 29% by the end of last season.
Poor shooting is what holds him back. One expert thinks he has stalled on offense, and another partly blames injuries for the shooting drop.

note: Both sites value him at 0 USD. He ranks 211 on Yahoo and 180 on ESPN, well outside the 144 players drafted in our league, and the notes give no reason to draft him. His only plus categories are steals and blocks (projected 1.2 and 0.9). Shooting and points are below average, and his projected minutes drop to 24 from 26.2 because of the usage and frontcourt crowd. Leave him on waivers. Early in the season, check whether he wins the fifth starter spot and whether Anthony Davis misses games, since that would give him back minutes and rim contests.
